contracts.name: Storage and confirmation
contracts.existing: One complete state per environment in IndexedDB, with localStorage fallback; transact snapshots memory, invokes a synchronous mutation and awaits one save.
contracts.must_preserve: No success feedback until all required commits are confirmed; no remote failure handled as a local-only success; no old local catalog promoted to SQL authority.
contracts.missing: Durable operation journal, server receipt reconciliation, per-entity versions and separation of local and server authority. busy is page-local only.

contracts.name: Sale with new customer
contracts.existing: createSale can append a customer, a sale, a receipt and an audit entry in one local save; email deduplication searches the current state.
contracts.must_preserve: Same customer ID on the sale; exactly one receipt for a collected sale; no sale or receipt lost or duplicated on retry.
contracts.split: Customer becomes SQL-owned; sale, receipt and current audit remain local. Two durable writes require recovery coordination, not memory rollback.

contracts.name: Subscription with new customer
contracts.existing: One operation can create customer, subscription, event, sale and receipt.
contracts.must_preserve: Customer/project/plan references, subscription event order, payment and receipt behavior.
contracts.split: Customer/project SQL ownership intersects local plans, subscriptions, sales and treasury; none of those financial collections may be migrated in this phase.

contracts.name: CSV, JSON and duplicate review
contracts.existing: Imports can create customers and financial records; JSON events can also update project userStats. Seen IDs and duplicate review remain local.
contracts.must_preserve: No regenerated IDs or duplicated records after uncertain acknowledgments; no partial SQL customer or project mutation hidden by per-event error handling.

contracts.name: Project children
contracts.existing: Project editor writes projects; user editor appends nested userStats; plan and time editors append separate local collections referencing the project ID.
contracts.must_preserve: Nested statistics and local plans/time logs remain attached to the same IDs; no project overwrite from an old local state.

contracts.name: Catalog deletions and historical lookups
contracts.existing: Delete guards inspect only this browser's sales, expenses, subscriptions, plans and treasury; historical labels and grouping also resolve against current catalog arrays.
contracts.must_preserve: An offline or second browser must never lose a referenced customer, currency, channel, product/version, brand, account or project.
contracts.missing: The server cannot see references held only in other browsers. Row versions alone cannot enforce referential integrity across that boundary. Archiving must retain resolvable identity and historical data.

contracts.name: Backup, restore and wipe
contracts.existing: Backup serializes the whole state; restore replaces the whole environment state; wipe assigns emptyState and saves directly outside transact.
contracts.must_preserve: No discarded records or dangling references, no old backup silently overwriting newer SQL revisions, and no destructive action affecting another environment.
contracts.scope_to_resolve: Once catalog rows are shared, restoring/wiping one browser no longer has the same scope as replacing its complete local state. Specify shared-catalog versus browser-local effects before activating split persistence.

contracts.name: Bootstrap and environment separation
contracts.existing: State version 1; missing fields are normalized; production and test environments use distinct local keys; boot catches load errors and renders the initial state.
contracts.must_preserve: Production/test separation on SQL foreign keys; transport or authentication failure must not be interpreted as an empty remote business; UI preferences and PIN stay local.

safer_transition_proposal.work: Define a versioned environment/workspace identity and perform explicit staged bootstrap reconciliation. Preserve existing IDs; report collisions and orphaned references without silently fixing them or overwriting server data.
safer_transition_proposal.data_rule: No automatic upload on load; no real data required for initial tests.

safer_transition_proposal.work: Implement normalized SQL catalogs with row versions and idempotent command receipts. Archive instead of physically deleting any remotely referenced catalog identity; retain historical versions needed by local lookups.
safer_transition_proposal.data_rule: No financial payload stored in SQL, including in operation receipts. A reference manifest alone cannot prove that offline browsers hold no references.

safer_transition_proposal.work: Introduce a durable browser operation journal. Prepare the local operation before the idempotent SQL request; reconcile an unknown SQL result by its stable operation ID; finalize local financial changes and journal status atomically in IndexedDB. Resolve pending operations on restart before allowing dependent writes.
safer_transition_proposal.data_rule: This is a recovery protocol, not an assertion of cross-store ACID. Test all interruption points and conflicts before activation; no success notification until both sides are confirmed.

safer_transition_proposal.work: Specify and test backup/restore/wipe scope for shared catalogs and local financial records. Proposed default: versioned backup with explicit catalog revision; restore is staged and conflict-checked, retains historical identities, and never blindly replaces newer shared rows.
safer_transition_proposal.decision: The treatment of shared catalog changes during restore/wipe needs to be explicit; preserving the old full-state browser replacement by directly splitting save is unsafe.

safer_transition_proposal.work: Run synthetic two-context, retry, crash/restart, SQL-outage, orphan-reference and backup tests before connecting the existing controls to SQL; then execute the 13-screen functional/visual regression with the feature enabled.
safer_transition_proposal.activation_gate: No activation until every mixed-operation interruption recovers deterministically without duplicates or loss.

tests_this_turn.limitations: The two failure models exercise the existing transact memory rollback with a modeled split save. They do not claim a real SQL or IndexedDB integration test, nor an existing production data-loss incident.

inventory.method: Static candidate read/write/call sites by textual pattern; includes views, closure writers and aliases. Not an AST proof or an exhaustive dynamic data-flow analysis.
